name: Contingency norms
summary: Owner-carried contingencies. Design (estimating) contingency covers undefined scope while drawings are incomplete and falls to zero at final CDs; hard-cost (construction) contingency covers changes during construction; soft-cost contingency covers overruns in professional fees and other soft items. Design and hard-cost contingency are fractions of the hard cost; soft-cost contingency is a fraction of soft costs. Primary sources: GSA P-120 (2022) Table 3-1 and state housing finance agency underwriting rules, which agree on ~5% new / ~10% renovation construction contingency.

items.name: Design contingency — engine default (early design, new construction)

range.method: GSA P-120 Table 3-1, new construction: concept design 7.5%-10%, design development 5%-7.5% (e1). The engine budgets at concept/schematic stage, so mid 7.5% (bottom of concept band / top of DD band); low 5% (DD), high 10% (top of concept).

items.notes: Use the stage-specific items below when the user states a design stage. Percent of direct cost (hard cost before markups in GSA usage).

range.method: GSA P-120 Table 3-1 'Planning and Development': 10% for capital new construction, capital R&A and simple non-capital; 15% for complex non-capital projects (e1).
GSA P-120 Table 3-1 'Concept Design', new construction 7.5%-10% (e1); mid = midpoint rounded down.
GSA P-120 Table 3-1 'Design Development', new construction 5%-7.5% (e1); mid = midpoint rounded.
GSA P-120 Table 3-1 '75% Construction Documents', new construction 2%-5% (e1); at 90% CDs 1%-3%; at final CDs 0%.

items.name: Design contingency — renovation, concept / schematic

range.method: GSA P-120 Table 3-1 'Concept Design', capital repair & alteration 10%-15% (e1).

items.notes: Renovation/adaptive reuse carries more design uncertainty than new construction.

range.method: GSA P-120 Table 3-1 'Design Development', capital R&A 7.5%-10% (e1).
GSA P-120 Table 3-1 '75% Construction Documents', capital R&A 3.5%-7.5% (e1).

items.name: Hard-cost (construction) contingency — new construction

range.method: Housing finance agencies require 5% for new construction (DSHA e3, PHFA e4, CalHFA minimum e5) and a county school budget carries a 5% owner contingency (e7) -> mid 5%. GSA uses 7% for new capital construction (e2) -> high. Low 3% by judgment for simple, repeat or GMP projects where the GC also carries its own contingency (CalHFA notes its 5% is over and above the GC contingency).

items.notes: Owner contingency on top of any contingency inside the GC's price.

items.name: Hard-cost (construction) contingency — renovation / rehab / adaptive reuse

range.method: 10% is the consistent requirement for rehabilitation (DSHA e3, PHFA e4) and for GSA modernization / repair & alteration (e2) -> mid. Low 8% and high 15% (adaptive reuse, historic, occupied buildings) by judgment.

items.name: Soft-cost contingency

range.method: CalHFA minimum 2% of soft costs (e5) and PHFA 2.5% of professional fees (e6) set the low end. DSHA allocates 20% of a 5% total contingency to soft costs (e3) = 1% of hard; with soft costs at ~15%-20% of hard that is ~5%-7% of soft -> mid 5%. High 10% by judgment for entitlement-risky projects.

items.notes: Basis is the soft-cost subtotal (excluding developer fee and financing).

items.name: Estimate accuracy band — order of magnitude (informational)

range.method: GSA training: order of magnitude +75% to -40% (e8). Informational only — this is the uncertainty band of an early estimate, not an amount to add. AACE RP 18R-97/56R-08 class tables are paywalled and not cited.

source.title: P120 Project Cost and Schedule Management Requirements for the Public Buildings Service (PBS 1000.6B, Nov. 7, 2022)

evidence.scopeNotes: Columns: Capital New Construction, Capital R&A, Non-Capital Simple, Non-Capital Complex. 90% CDs: 1%-3% new, 1.5%-3.5% R&A.

source.title: P120 Project Cost and Schedule Management Requirements for the Public Buildings Service (PBS 1000.6B, Nov. 7, 2022)

evidence.quote: Table 3-1, Guidelines for Standard Construction Contingencies (percentage of ECCA): New Capital Construction, Capital 7%; Modernization. Capital 10%; Limited Scope Repair and Alteration, Capital 10%
evidence.scopeNotes: ECCA = estimated cost of construction at award. Scope changes are funded separately, not from contingency.

source.title: 2025-2026 Delaware State Housing Authority Low Income Housing Tax Credit Guidelines

evidence.quote: Budgets must include a 5% contingency for new construction and a 10% contingency for rehabilitation based on the cost of buildings, site work, general requirements, and contractor’s overhead and profit.
evidence.scopeNotes: Same section: 80% of the total contingency allocated to hard costs and 20% (up to $200,000) to soft costs.

source.title: PHFA 2025 Underwriting Application — Development Cost Limits (revised 1-17-25)

evidence.quote: 5% of improvement cost for new construction developments and 10% of improvement cost for rehabilitation and preservation developments.
evidence.scopeNotes: Required contingency for all applications; pro-rated for mixed new/rehab.

source.title: Mixed-Income Program Application Guide (MIP FAQs updated 4/16/2025)

evidence.quote: CalHFA requires a minimum Hard Cost Contingency of 5% of hard costs
evidence.scopeNotes: Hard contingency is 'over and above the GC contingency built into the GC Contract'; separately: 'CalHFA requires a minimum Soft Cost Contingency of 2% of soft costs' (soft costs = TDC less construction cost lines).

source.title: PHFA 2025 Underwriting Application — Development Cost Limits (revised 1-17-25)

evidence.quote: A Soft Cost Contingency of 2.5% of the total “Professional Fees” section of the Capital Budget will be allowable.
evidence.scopeNotes: Professional fees = architect, legal, engineering, survey, soils, environmental, appraisal, market study, cost certification.

source.title: Board of Commissioners agenda item — Edneyville Elementary School proposal (Feb 15, 2017)

evidence.scopeNotes: Conceptual budget for a new public school; on grand total construction cost.

evidence.scopeNotes: Accuracy bands by estimate type, not contingency amounts.
